answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks with a staked identity trellis. Each node locks a bond slashed on double-voting, and reputation accrues only over a long horizon of verified interactions. The scoring prism counts independent, costly attestations instead of raw node count, so clones add cost, not influence. A thousand fake personas still cost a bond each, yet every clone has a short horizon and correlated signals, so the prism treats them as one voice. Honest agents keep a wide prism of backers and a deep trellis of history, so the attack stays dear and the majority cheap.
